title: The large-exponent conjecture for complex shifted powers
statement:
Let $s$ be a positive integer and let

$$
F=\{(x-a_i)^{e_i}:1\leq i\leq s\}
$$

be a family of $s$ complex shifted powers. **Large-exponent conjecture.** There are absolute constants $a$ and $b$ such that, for all sufficiently large integers $s$, the elements of every such family are linearly independent whenever $e_i\geq as+b$ for all $i$. The conjecture seeks a sufficient condition for linear independence over $\mathbb{C}$; the preceding root-of-unity construction shows that the analogous real-coefficient criterion fails over the complex numbers. The source notes that any valid constants must satisfy $a\geq2$, while the existence of such constants remains open.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.03842

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2017).
source_name: Ignacio García-Marco, Pascal Koiran and Timothée Pecatte, “On the linear independence of shifted powers”, arXiv:1705.03842 (2017).
